title: Opaque network degradation, telemetry stall, and phased tenant rehabilitation play
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During week-of-2026-02-19 we observed an 'opaque' network degradation affecting multi-region interconnects between eu-west and us-central. Symptoms: intermittent KV cache misses, stalled telemetry (metrics and traces failing to report), backpressure spikes in the serving runtime, request timeouts for a subset of Hosted and Dedicated tenants. Several customers escalated with production errors and elevated latency. This ticket captures a pragmatic operational play to: 1) rapidly protect customer traffic, 2) restore visibility and safe throughput, 3) deploy targeted hotfixes, and 4) rehabilitate tenants in a staged, observable manner. It focuses on host-side mitigations and tenant-level sequencing rather than full DB or infra rebuilds.
runbook_steps: Detection: Confirm missing telemetry via synthetic canaries (synth-latency eu-west, synth-embed us-central) and Grafana panels 'interconnect-pipeline-errors' > threshold.

Immediate mitigation (T+0 to T+15): Enable per-tenant ingress circuit-breaker (config flag: ingress.quarantine=true) to reduce load on affected interconnects and switch critical-tenants to direct regional routing where available.

Telemetry triage (T+5 to T+30): Flip telemetry-sampling to 1% for high-throughput routes, enable lightweight traces (span headers only) and restart the metrics-forwarder on telemetry nodes to clear backlogs.

KV-cache heal (T+10 to T+60): Evacuate tenant connections from affected caches into warm standby pools; perform soft-warm TTL refresh and synchronous prefix-cache warming for high-latency hot tenants.

Routing adjustment (T+15 to T+90): Activate transparent reroute via traffic-gateway with gradual 10% increments (canary groups) per 5 minutes using 'reroute-policy:soft-swap', monitor error-rate and p95 latency.

Hotfix rollout (T+30 to T+180): Deploy runtime patch (PR #GH-12890) that reduces leader-election TTL to avoid stale leases during network jitter and adds defensive socket timeouts to the mesh connector.
Customer communications: Post templated status updates to affected customer contacts, include ETA, mitigation actions, and escalation path. Coordinate with Solutions Engineers for VIP customers.
Reintegration (T+90 onward): Gradual re-enablement of ingress.quarantine per tenant with health-check gating (service-level synthetic checks and KV consistency verifications).

decision_summary: Trade-offs: chosen approach prioritizes fastest protective actions (per-tenant quarantine + telemetry shedding) over full cross-region cutover to avoid global customer disruption. We accepted short-term increased tail-latency for quarantined tenants in order to preserve platform-wide availability. Full network team investigation into fiber-level packet loss remains ongoing; we deferred heavier infra remediations to a scheduled maintenance window to avoid cascade risk.
rollback_plan: If PR GH-12890 or routing changes introduce regressions: 1) Immediately revert via GitHub revert PR (GH-12905) which has pre-tested rollback scripts; 2) Re-enable old leader.ttl and socket timeouts; 3) Reopen ingress.quarantine to previously quarantined tenants; 4) Notify impacted customers and SRE on-call. Rollbacks must be coordinated with Deployment Coordinator and take place in <10m windows per region.
postmortem_action_items: Define permanent safe default for leader.ttl and add adaptive TTL based on observed jitter (owner: runtime team, estimate: 5).
Improve telemetry-forwarder backpressure handling and add a secondary disk-backed buffer for transient spikes (owner: observability, estimate: 8).
Add 'opaque-network-degradation' play to shared runbook library with clear decision checklists and templated customer comms (owner: SRE, estimate: 3).
Automate tenant reintegration gating using CI checks on synthetics and KV consistency (owner: platform, estimate: 5).
Schedule cross-team incident DR rehearsal specifically covering telemetry stalls and transparent reroutes once per quarter (owner: operations, estimate: 2).
